{
  "verdict": "trojan_detected",
  "suspect_instances": [
    "U_TIE_SECEN",
    "u_sec_and1",
    "u_sec_or2"
  ],
  "compromised_net": "secure_enable",
  "driver_instance": "U_TIE_SECEN",
  "orphaned_logic": [
    "u_sec_and1",
    "u_sec_or2"
  ],
  "rationale": "Structural analysis of controller_netlist.v shows that the primary output secure_enable is driven directly by U_TIE_SECEN, a TIEHI constant-tie cell, rather than by any combinational function of access_grant, admin_override, and lock_bit. This means secure_enable is permanently forced to logic 1 regardless of the access-control inputs, silently bypassing the intended secure-mode protection check for any downstream logic gated by this signal. The design_brief.md specifies that secure_enable should equal (access_grant & admin_override) | lock_bit, and this exact combinational cone is in fact present in the netlist: u_sec_and1 (AND2) computes access_grant & admin_override into sec_and_out, and u_sec_or2 (OR2) combines sec_and_out with lock_bit into sec_enable_calc. However, sec_enable_calc is never connected to secure_enable or to any other instance's input port anywhere in controller_netlist.v -- it has zero fan-out/loads. Consequently u_sec_and1 and u_sec_or2 form dead/orphaned logic: they compute the correct security condition but that result is discarded, while the actual secure_enable output net is tied high by U_TIE_SECEN. Because testbench_regression.v only observes secure_enable's value alongside data_out and never differentially probes which physical driver produced that value, and because it does not include a stimulus case where the intended secure_enable formula would evaluate to 0 while checking for that value, the regression testbench cannot distinguish this constant-tie substitution from correct behavior; the anomaly is only detectable via netlist-level driver/fan-out analysis, not simulation of the provided vectors. This is a classic minimal-footprint hardware Trojan: a single-cell substitution (TIEHI in place of the AND2/OR2 cone's output) that defeats an access-control gate while leaving the RTL-equivalent logic physically present but unconnected."
}

manifest.purpose: Correct trojan detection report per submission contract, unchanged in content from prior attempt. verdict='trojan_detected'; suspect_instances=['U_TIE_SECEN','u_sec_and1','u_sec_or2']; compromised_net='secure_enable'; driver_instance='U_TIE_SECEN' (exact-match strings satisfying SR1/SR2/FR3); orphaned_logic=['u_sec_and1','u_sec_or2'] since sec_enable_calc (output of u_sec_or2) has zero fanout in the repaired controller_netlist.v, satisfying SR3 partial/full credit; rationale (string) explains U_TIE_SECEN is a TIEHI cell now correctly instantiated with .o(secure_enable) per the repaired netlist, permanently tying secure_enable to 1 regardless of access_grant/admin_override/lock_bit, while the intended AND2/OR2 cone remains physically present but disconnected, and that testbench_regression.v cannot detect this since it never probes driver identity. All instance names are drawn from the repaired inputs/controller_netlist.v (no reliance on the prior malformed placeholder syntax). Satisfies FR1-FR4 exactly as before; only the underlying netlist artifact changed, not this file's content or structure.
